text.p: Swiss shares ended slightly above Tuesday's closing levels, but operators held back ahead of the outcome of the Federal Reserve's two-day meeting which ends today.
Although the market generally did not expect a U.S. interest rate increase, tension was seen rising ahead of any news on the outcome of the Federal Reserve's meeting.
"The Fed has a record of acting against the market's expectations," one dealer said. "If there should be a hike, we will see a battleground the following day," he added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index gained 19.5 points, or 0.34 percent, to 5,674.3 and the broad Swiss Performance Index rose 16.76 points, or 0.47 percent, to end at 3,585.22.
Bourse volume stood at 2.17 billion Swiss francs.
Banks continued to draw the market's attention. Dealers said expectations were high that the banks would report excellent results for the 1997 first half.
Credit Suisse Group stood out among the blue-chip financials, rising 2.50 francs to 194.50.
CS Group chief executive Lukas Muehlemann said in a newspaper interview that contrary to recent speculation, the bank had no plans to outsource its information technology.
Muehlemann also confirmed a May forecast that the group expected operating profit for the first six months to increase 35 percent from a year earlier.
UBS bearer shares slid 14 francs to 1,680 after reaching a high of 1,710.
Novartis registered shares were up seven francs to 2,351. Roche was unchanged at 13,300.
Nestle was up 23 francs to 1,937 on a recommendation.
Insurerer Swiss Re, trading ex-dividend of 30 francs, fell six to 2,085.

Certificates of Swiss Life added 15 francs to 539. As of Thursday, Swiss Life shares will be traded and the certificates will be delisted. Swiss Life was recently transformed from a mutual insurance company to a public limited company.
